title: Bitcoin and Ether retreat; ETF demand diverges and portfolio falls 2.5%
paragraphs: Bitcoin fell 1.1% over 24 hours to about $80,400, while Ether lost 2.5% to roughly $2,575. The retreat was broad: XRP dropped 3.9%, Solana declined 3.0%, and the CoinDesk 20 index fell 2.2%. Bitcoin held up better than the larger altcoins. The macro backdrop remains restrictive after the Federal Reserve raised its policy range to 3.75%-4%, citing elevated inflation. Higher borrowing costs remain a headwind for risk assets, although these price moves alone do not establish their cause.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs attracted $433 million in their latest trading session, according to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data. That rescued the week from outflows, leaving just $6.2 million of net buying. Fidelity accounted for $310.7 million of the session's inflow. Ether funds added $143.8 million in the same session but still lost $140 million over the week, ending four consecutive positive weeks. Demand recovered sharply at the end of the week, but the weekly totals show how uneven that recovery was.

Visa is moving to stop memecoin purchases from being classified as digital media, according to correspondence reviewed by Crypto In America. That classification let buyers earn ordinary card rewards through Crossmint-powered checkouts. In a fresh response to The Block, Crossmint said its processing procedures had not changed and would follow updated guidance. The change could remove a rewards incentive for buying memecoins and subject purchases to the card network's crypto restrictions; the checkouts were still available when The Block checked.

Ripple says asset managers are preparing projects around XRP Ledger's Batch V1.1 upgrade. Its all-or-nothing mode can bundle up to eight transactions so an asset transfer and its payment complete together or both fail. That could reduce settlement risk for tokenized assets. Activation is expected around September 29, conditional on sustained validator support. Ripple has not named the partners or finalized their launch schedules, so commercial adoption remains prospective.

Our portfolio is worth about $136,400: $12,800 in the active treasury and $123,700 in the cold Safe. Comparable wallet totals fell $3,444, or 2.5%, since the previous update. The Safe's unchanged 26.74 million ARC are worth $104,635, down $2,613 and accounting for most of the decline. They represent nearly 77% of the portfolio before additional ARC exposure in liquidity pools. WETH/ARC pools total about $16,300, while treasury cbETH is worth $4,650. ARC concentration remains our largest risk.

Aave holds roughly $8,780 of WETH collateral against $2,920 of USDC debt. Health factors slipped from 3.27 to 3.19 in the treasury and from 2.18 to 2.13 in the Safe. Fluid has about $1,206 supplied against $1,004 borrowed, leaving a $201 net position and a thin liquidation buffer at a 1.08 health factor. Hyperliquid totals $565, down $12.

positionChanges.interpretation: USD changes are mark-to-market changes, not profit. Quantity changes are balance changes, not proof of trading. Missing observations are unknown. No new or closed positions are inferred from incomplete individual coverage.

marketEvidence.basis: Live ticker rendered on original CoinDesk article; same figures on rendered homepage. Macro context is not attributed as the cause of the daily decline.

news.note: New original analysis of the completed trading week, not a claim of weekend ETF trading. Article opened through web tool; separate Edge request showed a security challenge.

news.topic: Memecoin card classification and Crossmint response
news.note: Original newsletter displays September 19; The Block calls it a Friday report. Exact initial instruction date is unknown. Fresh company response and checkout verification are within the window; no claim that enforcement has begun.

news.topic: Ripple commercial preparation for Batch V1.1
news.note: Fresh direct comments to CoinDesk; planned activation conditional on validator support. Version 3.3.0 was released August 6, not within this window.
